summary: The note is an incident report on the response to the September 12, 2023 hurricane that hit Newport Haven, disrupting power and internet. It describes the 'Newport Haven model', which combined data analytics with grassroots networks, social media coordination, mobile health clinics, education programs, mental health services and interagency cooperation. It argues that community support and public health must be integrated into emergency planning, and mentions an upcoming Emergency Preparedness Forum.
one_line: Report on how Newport Haven combined community support, technology, public health and interagency coordination to respond to and recover from the September 2023 hurricane.
key_facts: On September 12, 2023, a hurricane ravaged the coastal town of Newport Haven, disrupting power and internet services and leaving the community isolated.
The 'Newport Haven model' used a tiered response mechanism that integrated real-time data analytics with a grassroots community network.
Coordinator James Buchanan led local emergency services in restoration operations and said at a September 13 press briefing, 'Coordination is paramount.'
The volunteer group Haven Helpers, organized by Sarah Metcalfe, used a dedicated app for citizens to report issues, offer assistance or request aid, enabling dynamic deployment of resources.
Tech companies introduced mobile charging stations and temporary internet hotspots to maintain communication for emergency teams and residents cut off from the grid.
Specialized task forces were designated to give tailored care to vulnerable groups including the elderly, children, and people with disabilities or chronic health conditions.
Dr. Eliza Martinez and her team established mobile health clinics for storm-related injuries and chronic patients without access to their regular healthcare facilities.
Starting October 5, 2023, Newport Haven Community College and local emergency services rolled out workshops on first aid, utility shutdown procedures and emergency evacuation protocols.

Jeffrey Liang, a resilience strategist and lecturer at Newport Haven Community College, said 'A knowledgeable community is a resilient community' and is working with local schools to add emergency preparedness to the curriculum.
Clinical psychologist Laura Gibson spearheaded mental health services, including counseling for signs of post-traumatic stress and support groups for ongoing peer support.

The Department of Health worked with the Office of Emergency Management, utility providers, telecommunication firms and educators to form an integrated support network that enabled rapid sharing of information and resources.
The Emergency Preparedness Forum on November 15, 2023 is expected to discuss cutting-edge technologies, expanded community education and stronger public health infrastructure.
